claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has a fine, regular lamellar microstructure of alternating soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
The FCC lamellae are Co/Cr/Fe-rich and the B2 lamellae are NiAl-rich.
The as-cast alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
The as-cast alloy has a proof stress of 75 MPa and a fracture stress of approximately 1.2 GPa at room temperature.
Catastrophic cracking and low ductility arise from the brittle nature of a continuous B2 network.
Hydrostatic pressure above about 20–22 GPa at 400–600°C will induce a localized B2-to-HCP or highly faulted transition in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The relevant pressure window is 22–41 GPa, based on the onset and completion pressures of an FCC-to-HCP transition in an HEA.
A temperature window of 400–600°C will overcome kinetic barriers without melting the alloy.
Helium provides an inert atmosphere that prevents oxidation during treatment.
Treatment for hours will be sufficient to complete the proposed phase transition.
High pressure can overcome kinetic barriers to an FCC-to-HCP transition by introducing stacking faults in a low-stacking-fault-energy HEA.
The pressure-induced transformed phase can remain metastably retained after decompression.
The proposed transition will disrupt the continuous B2 network while retaining the overall lamellar composite architecture.
High-density stacking faults in the B2 phase will impede crack propagation and promote dislocation storage.
The transformed or faulted B2 lamellae will promote dislocation cross-slip.
High stacking-fault energy and local disorder in the transformed B2 lamellae will enhance work hardening and reduce interfacial stress concentration.
Alternating soft FCC and hard B2 phases in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can produce substantial work hardening because B2 regions impede dislocation motion through FCC regions.

The treatment will reduce interfacial cracking, change fracture from intergranular or cleavage modes toward quasi-cleavage or ductile dimples, and increase uniform elongation without a proportional loss of yield strength.
Success requires pressure above the phase-transition threshold and a temperature high enough for transformation but low enough to avoid detrimental lamellar coarsening.
If conventional HIP at 200 MPa produces the same phase transformation and ductility improvement as extreme-pressure treatment, the claim that pressure above 20 GPa is required is falsified.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy as intrinsically low-ductility and catastrophically brittle, whereas the cited same-system evidence describes the as-cast lamellar alloy as having high ductility and ultra-high strain hardening. The adverse baseline is therefore not reconciled with the evidence used elsewhere.

The proposed transformation is analogized to a transition facilitated by low stacking-fault energy, but the claimed beneficial transformed state is attributed to high stacking-fault energy. The hypothesis does not distinguish whether the energy changes during treatment or reconcile the opposite roles.
